claims.text: High-entropy alloys commonly contain randomized atomic substitutions characteristic of disordered solid solutions.
A hybrid DFT and machine-learning approach using disorder-sensitive features will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than empirical or averaged-composition models.
DFT can provide detailed phonon-dispersion data for the disordered HEAs considered.
DFT can provide atomic-level disorder metrics suitable as machine-learning features.
Atomic-scale disorder and phonon-dispersion characteristics mediate phonon scattering in HEAs.
DFT-derived phonon spectra reveal vibrational modes and phonon-scattering pathways.
Machine learning using disorder-sensitive features can recognize subtle signatures of atomic disorder relevant to phonon transport.
Combining DFT phonon information with disorder-sensitive machine learning captures the effect of atomic randomness on phonon transport better than average-composition descriptors alone.
The hybrid approach will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 20% over conventional models.
Existing baseline prediction methods rely on averaged compositional or empirical descriptors without explicitly representing atomic-scale disorder and phonon dispersion.
The approach is primarily applicable to disordered substitutional HEAs.
The approach may not generalize to alloys with significant phase segregation or long-range order because its disorder metrics become less relevant.
TDTR measurements can be used to benchmark predicted thermal conductivity at relevant temperatures.
